negation agrees with subtraction from the additive identity at every swept raw, the asymmetric minimum included

MultiplicativeIdentity is (One, Zero) and is a two-sided identity for op_Multiply at every swept raw, exactly: the real product becomes a·2¹⁶ and the dual sum a·0 + b·2¹⁶, so the single rounding has no remainder
Constant(v) is (v, AdditiveIdentity) and Variable(v) is (v, MultiplicativeIdentity) at every swept raw — the two seeds differ in exactly one component, and Constant(One) is MultiplicativeIdentity
the forward-mode seed's defining property, read through op_Multiply: the dual part of Variable(x)·Variable(x)

The remark's claim that the fused form beats the quotient-rule form — which would round a/c, feed it through a product and round again — is exactly what the single-rounding oracle states

Legs.Subject: the divisor substitution is identical on both sides: Subjects.DualDivisor maps a zero REAL part — whatever the dual part carries — onto One, and the substituted point is pinned by dual.divide-refusals

the GENERIC branch refuses on its carrier's own terms: FixedDual<FixedSplit>.Divide by a divisor whose real part lies on the light cone throws the split algebra's DivideByZeroException, so the fallback path's refusal is the carrier's and not a second policy

Legs.Subject: FixedDual<FixedQuaternion>.op_Multiply via MultiplyQuaternion — the production dual quaternion behind FixedRigidTransform, whose every dual lane accumulates EIGHT leaf Q32 products across the dual seam before one rounding, under a two-clause gate (the symmetric 2²⁹ bound and the asymmetric rotation-below-2¹⁷ / translation-below-2⁴² bound)
Legs.Against: Oracles.DoublingDualProduct at two floors — the exact charged sums a·d + b·c formed lane by lane in BigInteger from the Cayley–Dickson doubling recursion, ONE Oracles.RoundDyadic at shift 16 per lane. The oracle knows nothing of the subject's term layout: its charges come from the recursion (a,b)(c,d) = (a·c − d̄·b, d·a + b·c̄) and its target key is an exclusive-or. The only shared convention is the lane permutation (X,Y,Z,W) ↔ (e₁,e₂,e₃,e₀), declared once in Subjects.QuaternionToDoublingLanes

Legs.Subject: ENVELOPE, and the reason this case exists: FixedDual<TValue>.op_Multiply is ONE member id over THREE kernels — MultiplyScalar, MultiplyQuaternion and the generic fallback — and the manifest cannot tell them apart. Before this case and dual.generic-carrier-two-roundings the id was covered by dual.mul-vs-oracle alone, which reaches only the scalar seam, so two of the three kernels were green without ever having run

the real block of the dual product is the plain Hamilton product of the two real parts, and the oracle forms it from the SAME doubling recursion quaternion.mul-vs-oracle's oracle uses — so the real lanes restate that case's statement at the dual carrier and the NEW content here is the dual block's eight-leaf fusion alone

FixedDual<FixedSplit>.op_Multiply — the GENERIC fallback, reached because FixedSplit is neither of the two JIT-folded house carriers: Real = a·c and Dual = (a·d) + (b·c) with the carrier's product formed TWICE and its wrapping add on top, so the dual part carries TWO roundings
Legs.Against: Oracles.DualOverQuadraticProduct at the (0, +1) relation — two independent Oracles.QuadraticMultiply results summed through Oracles.WrapToRaw, which is that discipline re-derived in BigInteger

Legs.Subject: ENVELOPE: this is the third and last kernel behind the op_Multiply member id, and the only one whose dual part is NOT fused. Its contract is deliberately weaker than the two house seams', and stating it here is what makes the fused seams' one-rounding claim a comparison rather than an assertion. No new type is introduced to reach it — FixedSplit already satisfies every constraint FixedDual<TValue> requires
the dual-number chain rule on f(x) = sqrt(x)·sin(x) + x²/(x+1) against an EXACT BigInteger derivative built from Oracles.EncloseSinCos, Oracles.IntegerSquareRoot and plain exact rational arithmetic
Legs.Against: sin(x)/(2√x) + √x·cos(x) + (x²+2x)/(x+1)², assembled in BigInteger: the sin/cos terms from Oracles.EncloseSinCos at raw x, sqrt(x) from Oracles.IntegerSquareRoot(x≠16) — matching FixedQ4816.Sqrt's own proven-exact floor bit for bit, so it is reused as an established fact rather than re-derived — and the polynomial term from an exact rational bounded directly at guard scale (no oracle at all). Widened by the kernel's 3/4 raw ULP SinCos envelope propagated through the one division (attenuated by 2·√x) and one multiplication (scaled by √x) those two terms perform, plus one full raw ULP for each of the four remaining fused single-roundings the chain performs (Sqrt(x)'s own Dual division, the sqrt(x)*sinD product's fused Dual rounding, x*x's Real rounding propagated into the quotient's numerator, and the quotient's own fused Dual rounding) — a safe, reasoned margin, not fitted to any observed output. No offline double computation anywhere
